title: Development and analysis of a ground impact attenuator for the re-entry capsule SARA.
author: Flávio José Silvestre
abstract: SARA (SAtellite for Re-entry in the Atmosphere) is a project in partnership between Brazil and Germany, of a capsule to conduce micro-gravity experiments in an orbit of 300 km. After the launch, the satellite must stay in orbit for approximately ten days and then be re-conducted to Earth. To reduce costs, one of the most important characteristics of this project is to be re-usable. In this way, it is necessary to develop a recovery system that protects the main structure of the capsule and also that supplies security conditions to the payload. The aim of this research work is to purpose a ground impact attenuator that will be put in the capsule's nose. The numerical and experimental analyse are also part of this work to be sure that all the required conditions will be satisfied.
